title: Open localized finite pullback is the pulled-back extension counit
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a scheme morphism, $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ an open immersion and $j':U'=T'\times_TU\hookrightarrow T'$ its inverse image, with $g_U:U'\to U$. Work on small pro-etale sites and their slice identifications [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Let $B$ be a finite commutative ring and use its canonical coefficient maps [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] and module tensor pullbacks [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $g_B^*$ for this pullback, $j^*,j'^*$ for restriction, and $j_!F=P_F^\#$ for the extension of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], with its adjunction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] and the unit-compatible slice sheafification comparison [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification]. Define $H=j'^*g_B^*j_!$. If $\epsilon:j_!j^*\to\mathrm{id}$ is the actual adjunction counit, then
$$\beta=j'^*g_B^*(\epsilon):Hj^*\longrightarrow j'^*g_B^*$$
is an isomorphism. Under the canonical identification $H\cong g_{U,B}^*$ from [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism], $\beta$ is exactly the canonical localized pullback comparison $g_{U,B}^*j^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^*g_B^*$. Its generator formula evaluates the summand indexed by $V\to U$ as the same section on $V$. For the actual adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$, the unit sends a section $s\in F(V\to U)$ to its generator in the summand indexed by $V\to U$, followed by sheafification. The counit $j_!j^*M\to M$ sends the generator in each such summand to the same section of $M(V)$.
